Title: The re‐emergence of hallucinogenic research
Authors: Begola, Matthew J.; Dowben, Jonathan S.
Abstract: Due to the intractability, at times, in the treatment of PTSD, clinicians and researchers continue to explore different options for treatment. This article discusses the renewed interest in hallucinogens for such treatment. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2025 APA, all rights reserved) (Source: journal abstract)

Title: "Psychedelic" effects produced by sensory overload
Authors: Ludwig, Arnold M.
Abstract: Presents preliminary results of a study indicating that approximately 24% of 46 normal adult Ss exposed to sensory overload reported a variety of subjective "psychedelic" effects. Ss were exposed to banks of flood lamps (light intensity of 40-70 ft-c) and taped sounds (SPL of 90-100 db.), in 2.5-hr sessions. Resulting effects pertained to perceptual distortions, disturbances in sense of time, "otherworldly" feelings, feelings of loss of control, somatic effects, and diminished reality testing. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2016 APA, all rights reserved)

Title: DPT as an adjunct in brief psychotherapy with cancer patients
Authors: Richards, William A; Rhead, John C; Grof, Stanislav; Goodman, Louis E; Di Leo, Francesco; Rush, Lockwood
Abstract: 30 24–71 yr old cancer patients suffering from psychological distress participated in a pilot project of individual psychotherapy that offered, over a 4 wk period, approximately 12 hrs of conventional verbal interaction and a single intensive drug-assisted therapy session that employed dipropyltryptamine (DPT), a short-acting psychedelic drug. The efficacy of the total therapeutic approach in enhancing the quality of life is indicated by the analysis of data from psychological tests (the Mini-Mult and the Personal Orientation Inventory) and independent ratings of 2 social workers on the Emotional Condition Rating Scale completed before and after the treatment intervention. The relative merits of DPT in comparison with LSD and the need to pursue a controlled study are discussed. (27 ref) (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2022 APA, all rights reserved)
Journal: Omega: Journal of Death and Dying

Title: Personality characteristics associated with psychedelic flashbacks in natural and experimental settings
Authors: Heaton, Robert K.; Victor, Ralph G.
Abstract: Compared MMPI profiles of 30 male psychedelic drug users with and without previous flashback experiences. MMPI differences enabled correct classification of the majority of both types of Ss. Controlling for differences which might be attributable to the flashbacks themselves, profiles associated with previous flashbacks still reflected more "loose," less reality-oriented thinking. Under experimental conditions involving mild sensory deprivation and the administration of either placebo or 50 mg ephedrine sulfate, Ss with MMPI evidence of loose thinking experienced significantly more psychedelic-like sensations, even when given instructions that tended to inhibit altered states of consciousness. Results are interpreted as suggesting that flashbacks are exacerbations of more stable psychopathology which occur in situations that tend to induce altered states of consciousness even without previous drug use. (29 ref) (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2025 APA, all rights reserved)

Title: Failure of outpatient treatment of drug abuse: II. Amphetamines, barbiturates, hallucinogens
Authors: Anderson, William H.; O'Malley, John E.; Lazare, Aaron
Abstract: Reports an attempt to engage abusers of nonopiate drugs in ongoing outpatient treatment. Continuing care (psychotherapy or hospitalization) was offered to 83 of the 208 persons who came to a 24-hr walk-in psychiatric clinic with reported problems of drug abuse. 9 returned once; 1 followed through with recommended treatment. 79% of a control group (N = 100), matched for age and sex from other diagnostic categories, returned as requested. Failure to generate therapy is considered in terms of: (a) patient motivation, (b) quantity and quality of treatment, (c) patient-therapist communication, (d) euphoria produced by drugs vis-a-vis therapy, and (e) ignorance of the cause of drug abuse. The last reason is deemed most plausible and worthy of further study. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2022 APA, all rights reserved)

Title: The science behind psychedelic therapy: Many questions remain about the formerly taboo chemicals that are speeding towards the clinic
Authors: Reardon, Sara
Abstract: In this paper, the author addresses the science behind psychedelic therapy. The author addresses the following questions: 1) what is a psychedelic? 2) how do these drugs work? 3) do psychedelics rewire the brain? 4) what else might these drug do? and 5) is it all a placebo effect. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2025 APA, all rights reserved)

Title: Mind and body in biological psychiatry
Authors: Alexander, Leo
Abstract: Claims that bodily influences on the mind and mental influences on the body which are applied in the practice of biological psychiatry involve the following interactions: (a) bodily nonverbal support through mild euphoriant medication or placebo; (b) stressful bodily challenges, e.g., by stimulating or hallucinogenic drugs; (c) extinction of conditioning and strengthening of unconditioned responsiveness, e.g., by ECT or specific antipsychotic drugs; and (d) new conditioning of bodily functions by verbal means, e.g., by psychotherapy, including hypnosis. Case histories illustrating these areas are described. (20 ref.) (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2018 APA, all rights reserved)
